topics.title: Chapter overview
topics.summary: A condition variable lets a thread wait for shared state to become useful without repeatedly polling it. The state remains the source of truth; the notification is only a prompt to check again. This chapter builds a bounded queue with explicit close semantics, then verifies that accepted values are drained before a consumer observes end-of-stream and that blocked producers can stop when the queue closes.

blocks.text: This chapter makes a bounded queue’s state machine explicit. The queue can be open, full, empty, or closed with remaining items to drain. Producers and consumers wait on predicates protected by one mutex. Closure changes state and wakes both groups. The design teaches backpressure and shutdown together because a queue that works only while every participant stays healthy is not a complete concurrent component.

topics.title: 18.1.1 Waiting with Predicates
topics.summary: A condition-variable wait uses a unique_lock so it can atomically release the mutex while waiting and reacquire it before returning to inspect state. The predicate form expresses the condition under the same mutex, such as queue not empty or queue closed. This prevents a notification from being treated as a durable message independent of state.

blocks.text: A condition variable is used with a mutex and a predicate over shared state. The waiting thread holds the mutex, checks whether it may proceed, and otherwise waits through an operation that releases the mutex and later reacquires it before returning. The predicate overload repeats the check as needed. The state, not the notification count, determines whether work is available. (CONDVAR)

blocks.text: For the consumer, the predicate is typically “closed or not empty.” After waking with the mutex held, it can distinguish a remaining item from a closed-and-empty terminal state. For the producer, the predicate is “closed or there is space.” A closed queue rejects new work even if capacity is available. These predicates encode different role permissions over the same state machine.

These predicates encode different role permissions over the same state machine.

blocks.text: Every field used by the predicate must follow the same synchronization discipline. Setting a plain closed flag outside the mutex while other threads read it inside the mutex is not sufficient. Either protect it consistently with that mutex or design a separately proved atomic protocol. Mixing approaches casually can create data races or lost state transitions.

Holding an unrelated required lock across the wait can still create a deadlock if the producer needs that other lock to make the predicate true. Review the complete dependency graph, especially when queue operations are called from code already holding component locks.

An empty string, zero integer, or null-looking payload may be a legitimate item and should not be overloaded as shutdown unless the domain explicitly reserves it. Ownership transfers through the returned value when an item is successfully removed.

topics.title: 18.1.2 Handling Spurious Wakeups
topics.summary: A wait can return even when the desired state has not become true, and another awakened thread can consume the state first. Therefore recheck the predicate in a loop or use the predicate overload that performs that loop. An if statement followed by a bare wait is not a complete substitute.

blocks.text: Notifications can also occur before a waiter begins waiting. A correct state predicate handles this because the waiter sees the already changed state and need not sleep. A design that relies on counting notifications instead of storing queue or readiness state can lose work. Use a semaphore when counted permits are the intended abstraction, not an undocumented imitation with condition variables.

blocks.text: A condition-variable wait can wake without the predicate becoming true. Even when a notification corresponds to a real state change, another thread may consume that opportunity before this waiter reacquires the mutex. Both cases require rechecking the predicate. An if around a raw wait is not an adequate general replacement for a predicate loop.

blocks.text: Notifications are not stored as ordinary messages for future waiters. If no thread is waiting, a notify does not create a token that a later waiter consumes. This is safe when the actual state change remains represented in the protected queue: a later consumer sees the nonempty predicate and never needs the old notification. Designs that rely on notification alone without durable state are vulnerable to missed progress.

blocks.text: Notify after modifying state under the mutex discipline. It is often useful to unlock before notifying to avoid waking a thread only to have it immediately block on the same mutex, but correctness depends on the protected state transition and predicate protocol, not on a universal rule that notify must always occur inside or outside the lock. Preserve the state object’s lifetime through the notification.

blocks.text: Use notify_one when one newly available opportunity should wake one suitable waiter, and notify_all for a global transition such as closure that may make every waiter eligible to stop. blocks.text: Tests should verify behavior through state transitions rather than depend on an exact scheduler order. Arrange known preconditions, release a gate, and verify eventual bounded completion under the outer harness. A test that sleeps for a millisecond and assumes a worker is now waiting can be flaky and fail to test the intended path. Where a deterministic seam is possible, expose the state transition instead of guessing timing.

topics.title: 18.2.1 Building Thread-Safe Queues
topics.summary: A blocking queue coordinates push and pop under one state invariant. The example stores a bounded deque, a closed flag, and two condition variables for not-empty and not-full conditions. Pop waits until an item exists or closure is visible; if closed and empty, it returns absence. Existing accepted items are drained after close.

blocks.text: Push rejects new values after closure. Moving a value out of the front should have a suitable exception contract so a failed move does not leave a partially consumed logical item. This generic teaching queue requires nothrow move construction. Container allocation during push can still fail, and callers must arrange closure so other threads are not stranded when a producer fails.

This generic teaching queue requires nothrow move construction. Container allocation during push can still fail, and callers must arrange closure so other threads are not stranded when a producer fails.

blocks.text: A thread-safe queue must define more than mutual exclusion around a container. Its contract includes capacity, insertion failure, removal failure, closure, draining, exception behavior, and ownership transfer. The teaching queue bounds the number of queued elements, rejects pushes after closure, and lets consumers drain already-accepted items before returning a terminal empty result.
rich: A thread-safe queue must define more than mutual exclusion around a container. Its contract includes capacity, insertion failure, removal failure, closure, draining, exception behavior, and ownership transfer. The teaching queue bounds the number of queued elements, rejects pushes after closure, and lets consumers drain already-accepted items before returning a terminal empty result.

blocks.text: The push parameter is taken by value. That means the caller’s argument may already have been copied or moved before the function discovers closure. A false return means the queue did not accept the item; it does not promise that a moved-from caller argument has been restored. This matters for unique resource owners such as accepted sockets. Choose a by-reference or returned-rejected-item design when preserving caller ownership after rejection is required.

blocks.text: The implementation requires nothrow move construction for its item type so removing an item and transferring it to a caller can maintain a simple state transition. The underlying deque can still allocate during insertion. A queue capacity measured in elements does not imply allocation-free operation or a strict byte bound. For a hard fixed-storage requirement, choose a bounded ring representation and define its object-lifetime behavior explicitly.

blocks.text: Closure is idempotent: repeated calls leave the same closed state and wake blocked participants. It is not the same as cancellation of already-running work. Once an item has left the queue, the consumer owns it and must follow its own completion or cancellation policy. The server architecture distinguishes queued connections from active connections for this reason.

blocks.text: Destruction requires participant quiescence. A queue object cannot safely disappear while producers or consumers still execute its methods or wait on its condition variables. The owner must close, make workers able to finish, join them, and only then destroy the queue. Declaring a queue near a worker vector is not enough; inspect reverse destruction order and partial-startup failure paths.

topics.title: 18.2.2 Applying Backpressure
topics.summary: Backpressure slows or rejects producers when downstream capacity is exhausted. A bounded queue blocks push while full, preventing unbounded memory growth from an indefinitely faster producer. The bound does not make the entire application bounded if items themselves own unbounded data or if other queues continue accumulating work.

A production API may also need try_push, deadlines, cancellation, or drop policies. Those behaviors should be explicit rather than hidden as arbitrary sleeps or silent overwrites.

blocks.text: Backpressure connects admission to available processing capacity. A blocking bounded queue slows producers when the queue is full. A nonblocking rejection policy returns immediately instead. A timed admission policy waits only within a declared deadline. Each can be correct for a particular system, but callers must know whether submission can block, fail, or consume their payload before acceptance.

blocks.text: Queue capacity is not the complete work-in-progress bound. With capacity q and w workers, up to q items can be queued while up to w more are actively processed. The accepting thread may temporarily own another item, and upstream buffers may retain additional input. A meaningful resource budget counts all these stages rather than quoting only the queue’s configured size.

blocks.text: Blocking a producer while it holds a resource needed by consumers can deadlock the system. For example, a producer that retains a global processing lock while waiting for queue space may prevent workers from completing their current items. Define lock and ownership boundaries before calling a potentially blocking submit operation.

blocks.text: When a worker fails, the system must decide whether to continue with reduced capacity, reject new work, close the queue, or abort the operation. If every consumer exits while a producer waits on a full open queue, no future dequeue can make progress. A failure path that closes and notifies the queue lets the producer observe terminal state instead of blocking forever.

blocks.text: A bounded queue controls retained work but does not by itself control per-item latency. A single item can stall in a blocking system call while the queue remains perfectly bounded. Pair admission limits with request deadlines and cancellation paths when the service requires bounded response behavior. Even then, ordinary operating-system scheduling prevents these teaching bounds from constituting a hard real-time guarantee.

reading.title: 18.2.2 Applying Backpressure
paragraphs: Backpressure slows or rejects producers when downstream capacity is exhausted. A bounded queue blocks push while full, preventing unbounded memory growth from an indefinitely faster producer. The bound does not make the entire application bounded if items themselves own unbounded data or if other queues continue accumulating work.

Define shutdown and overload separately. Closing wakes both producer and consumer waiters, while temporary fullness waits for space. A production API may also need try_push, deadlines, cancellation, or drop policies. Those behaviors should be explicit rather than hidden as arbitrary sleeps or silent overwrites.

blocks.text: The producer closes the queue on both success and a caught failure. The consumer also closes on failure so a blocked producer can wake and stop. blocks.text: Thread construction itself is another failure boundary. The closure guard is declared after the worker container and before any workers start. If a later thread creation fails, the guard closes the queue before the already-started workers are joined during unwinding. The guard does not cancel arbitrary user code; its guarantee relies on this queue’s closed predicate being part of every wait.

topics.title: Failure clinic — Race-free but permanently blocked
topics.summary: All queue fields are protected by the mutex, yet shutdown hangs. The owner requests stop on a jthread without closing the queue, so the worker’s condition-variable predicate remains false. There is no data race; there is a missing liveness transition. Add closure or a stop-aware predicate path and notify the relevant waiters.
